title: Inert-active orthogonal factorization in a symmetric infinity-operad
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and symmetric infinity-operads, inert edges and active edges as defined in [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction]. Let $P\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ be any symmetric infinity-operad in a fixed universe. Every edge $h:x\to z$ admits a coherent factorization $x\xrightarrow{i}y\xrightarrow{a}z$ with $i$ inert and $a$ active. Both classes contain the equivalences, are closed under composition, and are invariant under equivalence of arrows. For every inert $i:x\to y$ and active $a:u\to v$, the canonical map
$$\operatorname{Map}_P(y,u)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_P(x,u)\mathop{\times}^{h}_{\operatorname{Map}_P(x,v)}\operatorname{Map}_P(y,v),\qquad t\longmapsto(ti,at),$$
is an equivalence. The homotopy pullback uses postcomposition with $a$ and precomposition with $i$. Here $X\times_Z^hY$ is the space of triples $(x,y,\gamma)$, with $\gamma$ a path between the two images in $Z$, retaining all paths and higher simplices; explicitly it is $X\times_{Z,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,Z)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,Z}Y$. Equivalently, the space of fillers, including both triangular homotopies, of every coherent square with left side $i$ and right side $a$ is contractible. All arities, including zero and nullary active operations, are allowed.

proof.text: Write $p:P\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$. The definition of symmetric infinity operad in [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction] agrees clause for clause with that used in [lem-coef-symmetric-inert-active-orthogonality]: an inner fibration, cocartesian inert lifts, fibre Segal equivalences, and output mapping-space products. In the fixed universe $P$ is small; alternatively regard that universe as the small one inside a containing universe. Apply the latter existing node to obtain the coherent triangle $h\simeq ai$ for every edge $h$, and its displayed mapping-space equivalence for every inert $i:x\to y$ and active $a:u\to v$. The comparison sends $t$ to $(ti,at)$ with the associativity homotopy between $a(ti)$ and $(at)i$, exactly as required here. This uses only the existing node's statement, with no simultaneous functorial choice of all factorizations asserted.

proof.text: For pointed maps $f:A_*\to B_*$ and $g:B_*\to C_*$, activeness gives $(gf)^{-1}(*)=f^{-1}(\{*\})=\{*\}$. If $f,g$ are inert and $c\ne *$, its unique preimage $b$ under $g$ is non-basepoint and has a unique preimage under $f$; thus $gf$ is inert. Bijections satisfy both conditions. A simplicial functor sends the inverse edge and its two inverse triangles to inverse data, so an equivalence of $P$ maps to an isomorphism of finite pointed sets. Such an edge is $p$-cocartesian: for each $\Lambda_0^n$ lifting problem with this distinguished edge, [lem-cbc-inner-fibration-equivalence-outer-horn-lift] supplies exactly the filler required by [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. It is therefore inert as well as active. For two composable inert edges choose a composition triangle by the inner-horn axiom. Its composite is $p$-cocartesian by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality], and its base map is inert by the finite-set calculation. Hence inert edges are closed under composition. Active edges are precisely edges whose images are active, as explicitly defined in [lem-coef-symmetric-inert-active-orthogonality], so their closure follows from the same base calculation. The cancellation theorem applies because $p$ is an inner fibration between quasicategories; no cocartesian lift of an active base arrow has been assumed.

source.place: Opposite dual of Proposition 2.4.1.7 and equivalence outer-horn lifting; explicit derivation of the closure clauses also recorded in Corollary 5.2.8.13.

proof.text: Let $f:x\to y$ and $f\prime:x\prime\to y\prime$ be equivalent objects of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,P)$. Evaluation of an inverse and its two inverse triangles at each endpoint gives equivalences $e:x\to x\prime$ and $d:y\to y\prime$. The equivalence transformation is a map $\Delta^1\times\Delta^1\to P$. Its two triangles have a common diagonal $k:x\to y\prime$, and say $k\simeq df$ and $k\simeq f\prime e$. If $f$ is inert, Step 2 shows that $d,e$ are cocartesian; the first triangle makes $k$ cocartesian, and cancellation of $e$ in the second triangle makes $f\prime$ cocartesian, both by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]. In the base these same triangles give $p(f\prime)=p(d)p(f)p(e)^{-1}$, because simplices in an ordinary nerve are commuting diagrams. Relabelling the source and target by these pointed bijections preserves both the singleton non-basepoint fibres and the condition that no non-basepoint is sent to the basepoint. Thus $p(f\prime)$ is inert when $p(f)$ is inert and active when $p(f)$ is active. This proves preservation of each edge class by an equivalence of arrows; apply the same argument to the inverse transformation for the converse. Every choice of composite in Step 2 is likewise covered by this argument.

source.place: Definition 5.2.8.1 and Remark 5.2.8.2; arrow-equivalence invariance expanded using the two triangles of a coherent square and cocartesian cancellation.

proof.text: Put $X=\operatorname{Map}_P(x,u)$, $Y=\operatorname{Map}_P(y,v)$ and $Z=\operatorname{Map}_P(x,v)$. A point of $X\times_Z^hY$ is a top arrow $b:x\to u$, a bottom arrow $c:y\to v$, and a specified path $H:ab\simeq ci$. The path-space convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], with $Y$ in place of its specified point, gives exactly $X\times_{Z,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,Z)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,Z}Y$ degree by degree. The homotopy fibre of the comparison in Step 1 over $(b,c,H)$ consists of $t:y\to u$, paths $ti\simeq b$ and $at\simeq c$, and their compatibility with $H$, retaining all higher simplices. This is the coherent filler space, whose contractibility is precisely the last clause of [lem-coef-symmetric-inert-active-orthogonality]. Thus the two formulations in the item use the same homotopy data. There is no nonempty-arity restriction: the cited theorem includes arity zero, pointed bijections still satisfy the two base conditions for the one-point set, and $\langle0\rangle\to\langle n\rangle$ is active for every $n$, covering nullary operations whenever they exist in $P$.

lean.statement: theorem operadic_inert_active_factorization {P : SSet.{u}} (p : P ⟶ finStarBase.{u}) (hp : IsSymmetricInfinityOperad p) : (∀ h : Δ[1] ⟶ P, ∃ τ : Δ[2] ⟶ P, stdSimplex.δ 1 ≫ τ = h ∧ IsSymmetricInertEdge p (stdSimplex.δ 2 ≫ τ) ∧ IsActiveEdge p (stdSimplex.δ 0 ≫ τ)) ∧ (∀ e : Δ[1] ⟶ P, IsEquivalenceEdge P (SSet.yonedaEquiv e) → IsSymmetricInertEdge p e ∧ IsActiveEdge p e) ∧ (∀ τ : Δ[2] ⟶ P, (IsSymmetricInertEdge p (stdSimplex.δ 2 ≫ τ) → IsSymmetricInertEdge p (stdSimplex.δ 0 ≫ τ) → IsSymmetricInertEdge p (stdSimplex.δ 1 ≫ τ)) ∧ (IsActiveEdge p (stdSimplex.δ 2 ≫ τ) → IsActiveEdge p (stdSimplex.δ 0 ≫ τ) → IsActiveEdge p (stdSimplex.δ 1 ≫ τ))) ∧ (∀ e f : Δ[1] ⟶ P, AreNaturallyEquivalent e f → (IsSymmetricInertEdge p e ↔ IsSymmetricInertEdge p f) ∧ (IsActiveEdge p e ↔ IsActiveEdge p f)) ∧ ∀ i a : Δ[1] ⟶ P, IsSymmetricInertEdge p i → IsActiveEdge p a → IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (operadicDiagonalComparison i a) ∧ ∀ s : (operadicOrthogonalityDiagrams operadicOrthogonalityLeft operadicOrthogonalityRight i a) _⦋0⦌, IsContractible (homotopyFiber (operadicDiagonalComparison i a) s)
